newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian cabinet approves transport reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Italian cabinet approves transport reform bill.

text.p: A bill put forward by transport minister Claudio Burlando to restructure the Italian cargo transport industry was approved by the Italian cabinet last week.

"In ten years time our goods will no longer be able to leave Italy for Central Europe on wheels; we will no longer be able to serve the richest European markets with road transport; we will no longer be able to truck air cargo to Frankfurt or any other central European airport,' Burlando told an industry and press meeting on Thursday explaining the need for reforms.
The bill aims to provide incentives to reduce road transport replacing it with rail, sea and air transport.

It will try and exploit intermodality to help speed the transfer of a significant share of road traffic to other transport forms, increase highway safety, improve the environment and optimise road transport supply.

"The proposal is entirely new and is the prelude to a comprehensive restructuring of the entire Italian transportation sector in line with European Union norms," said transportation undersecretary Soriero.

Burlando said three additional transport sector bills will be added to the calendar by June 1997. These are for Alitalia privatisation, intermodal transportatioon and the definitive refoprm of the port system.

"By June 1997 the two government proposals regarding local and public transport and the reform of Civilavia (the transport ministry's civil aviation office) must be passed by parliament," Burlando stated. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
